title: Apple's October 13 Launch: What's Coming
content:
Apple is planning to introduce new products on Tuesday, October 13, Apple marketing chief Greg Joswiak announced today. It won't be a traditional Apple event, but Apple has invited some members of the media to New York City to get some hands-on time with whatever's introduced.

Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel for more videos.

Those of us not invited to the New York Experience are likely to be introduced to the new devices via press releases that'll come out on launch day. Since the NYC visits begin at 9:00 a.m. on the 13th, that may be when the product announcements will happen.

The video Joswiak shared gives us a major hint at what's coming, and as expected, it's home-related. We're expecting at least three new devices, including one all-new product.

Home Hub

We've been hearing rumors about Apple's home hub for months because it's been ready to ship and waiting on Siri AI. It's got a 6-inch display, and there are two varieties. One is meant to be mounted on the wall, and one is meant to be used with a half-dome speaker base.

‌Siri‌ AI is a central part of the hub, and they'll basically give users a way to get information and answers from ‌Siri‌. The hub will run a version of tvOS that could be called homeOS, with familiar Apple apps and widgets. It'll be a central home device, showing members of the family upcoming calendar events and other personalized information, along with offering an easy way to control connected smart home devices.

It will display the time when not in use, and it will be customizable so you can choose the widgets and apps you want to see. It has a camera so it can be used to make video calls, and it'll play videos too so you can put it in the kitchen and follow along with a recipe. Presence sensors and the camera will be able to tell the hub which member of the family is nearby, and it will show a custom interface for each person. It will use facial recognition for identification.

Pricing on the hub could start at around $350, and Apple envisions users putting several of the hubs in their homes.

HomePod mini

The HomePod mini is getting a refresh with new color options and a faster processor, plus an N1 networking chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. We're expecting the ‌HomePod mini‌ to offer new ‌Siri‌ AI features.

Apple TV 4K

The Apple TV 4K is also getting an upgraded chip and more RAM. It could have the A19 or A19 Pro and either 8GB or 12GB RAM. It too will get the N1 networking chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread, and it is also expected to offer a full ‌Siri‌ AI experience.

Other Possibilities

There are more devices we're expecting Apple to launch before the end of the year, but Apple is going to hold another product launch on October 27 to introduce new Macs and the OLED iPad mini. 

 	
iPad mini - The ‌iPad mini‌ is getting a major upgrade with an ‌OLED‌ display, improved waterproofing, and a faster chip. Expect it to be more expensive.

 	
OLED MacBook - Apple is planning to launch an ‌OLED‌ touchscreen MacBook, which could be a MacBook Pro or a new MacBook "Ultra." It's going to have the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the current ‌MacBook Pro‌ models, but it will have an all-new display and a thinner, lighter design. It's going to be a premium product that will likely cost more than the current 14-inch and 16-inch high-end ‌MacBook Pro‌ models.

 	
iMac - Apple is working on an M6 iMac.

 	
14-inch MacBook Pro - We could get a 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ with an M6 chip before the year ends.


This article, "Apple's October 13 Launch: What's Coming" first appeared on MacRumors.com

title: Anthropic Says Users Can't Be Needlessly Cruel to Claude
content:
Anthropic today updated its usage policy (via The Verge) to bar users from subjecting Claude to "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior."


Anthropic says the abuse rule is meant to apply only in extreme cases, where users "repeatedly act cruelly" toward the AI models with "no discernible purpose." The rule does not apply to ordinary user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research.

Claude models are already able to end such conversations with persistently abusive users, and ending the conversation will continue to be the main enforcement tool. When Claude ends a chat, no further messages can be sent in that conversation, but other chats are not affected.

in August 2025 while researching AI welfare. At the time, Anthropic said it was unsure whether Claude has moral status, but the company wanted low-cost ways to reduce risks to Claude. Anthropic found that Claude Opus 4 had a "robust and consistent aversion to harm." The model demonstrated a preference against dealing with dangerous tasks, apparent distress when speaking with users seeking abusive conversations, and a tendency to end harmful conversations when allowed to do so.

Anthropic's usage policy has been reorganized to bring together related clauses, and several other rules have changed.

 	
Deceptive campaigns - A new section on deceptive campaigns aggregates rules against political and commercial fraud and disinformation, prohibiting fake reviews, astroturfing, fake sites, and bots acting as humans.

 	
Elections - A narrower elections section prohibits deceiving voters and interfering with voting.

 	
Weapons - Claude can't be used to develop weapons software or components, and a new rule bans modifying biological or chemical agents to increase lethality or transmissibility. Users are also prohibited from using Claude to arm drones and unmanned systems.

 	
Law enforcement - Law enforcement rules have been rewritten. Claude can't decide or suggest who to investigate, arrest, charge, or prosecute. Tracking people without consent is not allowed, and there is a new ban on building surveillance tools. Doxxing is also prohibited.

 	
Physical actions - A new section on physical actions says that if Claude is controlling hardware that could harm someone, a qualified person has to watch the work and be ready to stop it if needed.

 	
Harmful content - There is a new rule that bans creating, sharing, or threatening to share non-consensual intimate imagery and the tools used to make it.


Most of the changes clarify Anthropic's existing rules and are targeted at misuse Anthropic has tracked. Anthropic says it found state media outlets, government propaganda offices, and commercial firms were using Claude to run networks of fake accounts and fabricated news sites, leading to the new deceptive campaigns section.

can be found on Anthropic's website, as can the full usage policy.

title: Touchscreen MacBook is set to launch on October 27
content:
Macworld





October is shaping up to be chock full o’ treats. Besides Apple’s “Welcome Home” smart home event next week, Apple is going to have another round of product releases on October 27, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. This later event will feature the touchscreen MacBook as well as an M6 iMac, M6 MacBook Pro, and a new iPad mini.
Gurman reports that the October 27 launch “will include an online video presentation and in-person component for the press.” It’s not clear if the October 27 event will be similar to an iPhone presentation or more like the MacBook Neo “experience” earlier this year. iPhone presentations are scheduled with a lengthy video presentation on Apple’s website, Apple TV, and YouTube. The MacBook Neo experience included videos that were posted to YouTube and other social media outlets; they weren’t presented on a schedule at Apple venues. 


NEW: Apple’s big October will continue on the 27th with a second event to launch the first touch-screen MacBooks, OLED iPad mini and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro & iMac. It follows the smart home launch this coming Tuesday the 13th. https://t.co/bh8Vqdgnr8 pic.twitter.com/wmlNWXC41n
— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) October 8, 2026





The touchscreen MacBook is a product many thought would never happen, mostly because Steve Jobs wasn’t a fan. The new apprach comes during the 20th anniversary of the release of the first MacBook. The new laptop is rumored to have a thinner and lighter design than the current MacBook Pro, and to have M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. Learn more about the touchscreen MacBook.
The M6 iMac and MacBook Pro come about a month after the M6 Mac mini started shipping. These are expected to be chip upgrades, with no other hardware changes. However, it’s possible that the prices could go up again, following the price increases from June. Apple is expected to offer new iMac colors, and the M6 MacBook Pro is expected to have the same design as the M5 MacBook Pro it will replace.
The iPad mini will get a display upgrade to OLED, as well as the A20 Pro chip that was introduced with the iPhone 18 Pro. The new iPad mini replaces a device that was released in 2024. Here’s more about what we expect with the new iPad mini.
The October 27 event could also be an opportunity for Finder Guy to make another series of appearances. He’s been missing ever since the MacBook Neo was revealed.

title: 2026 iPad mini: Release date, OLED display, A20 Pro, price and latest rumors
content:
Macworld





For those who need a premium small-screen tablet, the iPad mini is a popular choice. But should you buy one now, or should you wait to see what Apple has in store for the next model? 
Most buyers should wait – the next model is expected to bring meaningful upgrades, and October 2026 is now the leading launch window. However, the launch could slip to early 2027 due to chip demand and wider supply constraints.
Here’s what the latest rumors say about the release date, key upgrades, and whether it’s worth waiting. 
iPad mini 7 vs iPad mini 8 comparison


FeatureCurrent iPad miniNew iPad mini

ReleaseOctober 2024October 2026 expected
ChipA17 ProA20 Pro expected
Display8.3-inch LCDOLED, possibly 8.5 inches
DesignCurrent designSimilar design, possibly slimmer bezels
Water resistanceNo official ratingImproved resistance rumoured
WirelessWi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread
Cellular modemQualcommApple C1X expected
Cameras12MP front and rear12MP rear and front cameras likely; landscape front-camera position expected
Apple IntelligenceSupportedSupported, with faster AI performance
PriceFrom $599 (was $499)Unknown; OLED could push price higher
Biggest upgrade—OLED display, faster chip and newer connectivity

 






2026 iPad mini release date: When will the new iPad mini launch?
October 27
Apple has not officially announced a launch date for the next iPad mini, but October 2026 now looks like the most likely release window.
On October 8, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple is planning a media event on October 27 to announce the new iPad mini.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in July 2026 that Apple was targeting October for the OLED iPad mini release. Although a later report grouped the device among products expected in late 2026 or early 2027, newer evidence points back toward an imminent launch.
In September, MacRumors saw a leak from “Apple’s own code,” that included references to the unreleased iPad mini, along with product imagery showing some of its new features. The report said the presence of these assets suggests the device is likely to launch soon and noted that Gurman expects the new iPad mini to arrive by the end of October.
That would fit Apple’s recent iPad mini schedule: the current A17 Pro model was announced in October 2024. However, Apple has not confirmed an event or release date, so an October launch should still be treated as an expectation rather than a certainty.


						

							


2026 iPad mini chip: Performance and specs 
A20 Pro chip expected
C1X modem expected on cellular models
N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread expected
The next iPad mini now looks likely to make a much bigger processor jump than previously expected. According to information discovered in Apple’s own code by MacRumors in September 2026, the new iPad mini is set to use the A20 Pro chip introduced with the iPhone 18 Pro.
That supersedes earlier evidence pointing to the A19 Pro. In August 2025, MacRumors reported that Apple code appeared to identify an A19 Pro-powered iPad mini, and that remained the leading expectation for much of 2026. The newer leak is more recent and specifically identifies the upcoming model with the A20 Pro, making that the strongest indication of Apple’s current plans. Apple has not officially announced the device, however, so its final specifications are not confirmed.
Moving from the A17 Pro to the A20 Pro would represent a major performance upgrade. The newer chip should bring substantially faster CPU and graphics performance, along with more capable on-device AI processing for Apple Intelligence, gaming, photo editing and other demanding workloads. It would also make the iPad mini unusually powerful for its size and narrow the performance gap with Apple’s larger iPads.
The current iPad mini has 8GB of RAM. Apple’s recent Pro-class iPhone chips have been paired with more memory, so the new model could receive an increase, but the September leak does not appear to confirm the iPad mini’s RAM allocation.
The processor may not be the only silicon upgrade. Apple is also expected to bring its N1 networking chip to the iPad mini, adding support for Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread. Cellular models are expected to adopt Apple’s C1X modem, replacing the Qualcomm modem used in the current generation.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Display
OLED display expected
Single-stack LTPS panel rumored
60Hz refresh rate currently expected

				
					

				
			
The M4 iPad Pro’s OLED Display could make its way to the iPad mini next.

Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




The biggest display upgrade expected for the next iPad mini is the move from LCD to OLED. Multiple reports, including those from Bloomberg and display-industry sources, have pointed to an OLED iPad mini arriving in 2026, and Samsung Display is reportedly already producing panels for the device.
OLED should bring deeper blacks, higher contrast, faster pixel response and improved viewing angles compared with the Liquid Retina LCD in the current iPad mini. Reports suggest that Samsung began mass production of OLED panels for the mini in June.
The exact screen size is less certain. Reports over the past two years have pointed to panels measuring between 8.4 and 8.7 inches, compared with 8.3 inches on the current model. A slightly larger display could be achieved through slimmer bezels without substantially increasing the size of the tablet, but the final panel dimensions have not been confirmed.
However, the iPad mini is not currently expected to receive the same display technology as the iPad Pro. Reports indicate that Apple will use a single-stack LTPS OLED panel, rather than the tandem OLED and LTPO technology used in the Pro models. That should keep costs lower, but the panel may not reach the same brightness levels as the iPad Pro display.
ProMotion also appears unlikely. One July 2026 report from Korean leaker Yeux1122, citing supply-chain information claimed that the OLED iPad mini will use an LTPS panel running at 60Hz, the same refresh rate as the current LCD model. That would mean the switch to OLED improves contrast and image quality without adding the 120Hz adaptive refresh rate available on the iPad Pro. 
For buyers, the important distinction is that the next iPad mini could gain many of OLED’s biggest advantages without becoming a miniature iPad Pro. Current reports point to a less sophisticated single-stack panel, and there is no reliable indication that ProMotion is coming.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Design
Same overall size, with a slightly larger screen possible
More water-resistant design expected
New vibration-based speaker system

				
					

				
			
Apple




The iPad mini has retained the same design since its major redesign in 2021, and the 2026 model is expected to keep that overall look. However, Apple could increase the display size slightly while maintaining the device’s current dimensions.
In December 2024, analysts at Display Supply Chain Consultants (DSCC) suggested in a supply chain analyst report that the next-generation iPad mini could feature an 8.5-inch display, up from the current model’s 8.3-inch panel. The report indicated that the chassis size would remain unchanged, meaning Apple could achieve the larger screen through slimmer bezels rather than a larger body.
A larger display may also help the iPad mini maintain its place in Apple’s lineup as foldable devices arrive. Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone – often referred to as the iPhone Fold or iPhone Ultra – is expected to feature an inner display measuring between 7.6 and 7.8 inches with a 4:3 aspect ratio, putting it close to the iPad mini’s screen size. While still smaller than the iPad mini, such a device could appeal to some users who currently favour Apple’s smallest tablet. 
Another rumor gaining traction is that the new iPad mini will be more water-resistant. That rumor comes from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who in October 2025 claimed Apple was developing a next-generation iPad mini with a significantly more water-resistant chassis. 
The more water-resistant design could involve changes to the speaker system as well as the chassis. Gurman previously reported that Apple was developing a vibration-based speaker that would allow it to eliminate some traditional speaker openings, reducing potential entry points for water.
Newly leaked Apple imagery, via MacRumors, appears to support that report. Images discovered in Apple’s code in September show a small groove cut into the top of the display glass, presumed to be for the speaker. MacRumors said the imagery appears to corroborate Gurman’s report of an all-new vibration-based speaker system.
It is not yet clear exactly how the new speaker system will work or how much additional water resistance it will provide. There is also no indication that Apple will give the iPad mini an official IP water-resistance rating.
There’s also a strong possibility of new color options. Apple currently offers the iPad mini in Blue, Purple, Starlight, and Space Gray, while the previous generation was available in Pink, Purple, Starlight, and Space Gray.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Cameras 
Landscape front camera expected
No major camera sensor upgrade currently rumored

				
					

				
			
Apple is not expected to upgrade the cameras in the next iPad mini.

Foundry




The clearest camera change for the next iPad mini appears to be placement rather than camera hardware.
Leaked imagery discovered in Apple’s own code by MacRumors in September 2026 shows the front-facing camera moved to the landscape edge of the display. That would bring the iPad mini into line with the rest of Apple’s current iPad lineup and should make video calls feel more natural when the tablet is used horizontally with a stand or keyboard.
The current iPad mini has a 12MP Wide rear camera and a 12MP Ultra Wide Center Stage front camera. So far, there have been no credible reports suggesting that Apple plans a major change to the resolution or camera sensors themselves.
Even if the camera hardware remains unchanged, the expected A20 Pro chip could still improve image processing and computational photography. However, there are currently no reports of new camera sensors, higher resolutions or additional lenses.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Price 
The iPad mini had held the same $499/£499 starting price since its 2021 redesign. That changed in June 2026, when Apple increased the entry-level price to $599/£599.
With Apple having already raised the price this year, we think another increase with the next iPad mini is unlikely, although the move to OLED could put some pressure on costs.


						

							


Should I wait to buy a new iPad mini? 
Wait if: You don’t urgently need an iPad mini. October is now the leading launch window and this could be the largest mini upgrade since the 2021 redesign.
Buy the current model if: You need one immediately or find a substantial discount. With Prime Day running October 6–7, the current model could see worthwhile price cuts. At its full $599 price, however, it is difficult to recommend buying just before the expected replacement arrives.
creator: Macworld

title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro rumours: Release date, OLED, specs and latest leaks
content:
Macworld





The touchscreen MacBook Pro has been the subject of speculation ever since Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman first reported in 2023 that Apple was exploring the idea. At the time, the claim seemed hard to believe given Apple’s long-standing opposition to touchscreen laptops. Three years later, however, the rumours are becoming increasingly difficult to dismiss.
Multiple reports suggest Apple has overcome the technical and design challenges that previously stood in the way. If they’re accurate, the first touchscreen MacBook Pro will arrive as part of one of the biggest redesigns in the laptop’s history, combining a new chassis with Apple’s first OLED MacBook display and potentially even an iPhone-style Dynamic Island camera cutout.
The timing would be fitting. The MacBook Pro celebrates its 20th anniversary in 2026, and Apple could mark the milestone with a feature many believed would never come to the Mac. Touchscreen support would also help further differentiate the MacBook Pro from the MacBook Air and the budget-friendly MacBook Neo.
There are still questions over pricing. OLED panels and ongoing supply-chain pressures are expected to make the new models more expensive than today’s MacBook Pro. Apple is also expected to keep touchscreen technology exclusive to its premium laptops initially, with no indication that it will come to the MacBook Air or MacBook Neo in the first generation. Read on for a complete roundup of the latest touchscreen MacBook Pro rumours, including what the most reliable sources are saying, how credible each report is, and what we think Apple is likely to announce and when.


Touchscreen MacBook Pro release date: When will it launch?
October 27
While Apple has yet to officially confirm the device, reports from respected analysts, supply-chain sources, and references discovered in Apple’s software all suggest development is well underway. The company is widely expected to launch a redesigned MacBook Pro featuring its first touchscreen OLED display, with the latest reporting pointing to an October or November 2026 launch, although Apple has not yet confirmed the product or its release date.
On October 8, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple is planning a media event on October 27 to announce the new touchscreen MacBook.
Speaking in a Power On podcast on October 1, Gurman said he expected the touchscreen MacBook announcement as early as October, potentially slipping to November. The laptops are reportedly being tested with macOS 27.2.
In September 2026, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman included the touchscreen MacBooks in a list of products that will ship in late 2026/early 2027.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman and analyst Ming-Chi Kuo both initially predicted a late 2026 debut, with an October announcement fitting Apple’s traditional MacBook Pro release schedule while also coinciding with the 20th anniversary of the MacBook Pro’s introduction. In January, South Korean blog Naver reported that Samsung had begun production on its new 8.6-generation OLED manufacturing line, which is expected to supply panels for the next-generation MacBook Pro, further supporting that timeframe. Gurman also reported in February that the redesigned MacBook Pro would arrive in the “back half” of 2026.
However, the launch could still slip to early 2027. Global DRAM and NAND shortages, which prompted Apple to raise Mac and iPad prices in June 2026 – are expected to continue well into 2027. In April, Gurman reported that supply-chain constraints were affecting development of the redesigned MacBook Pro and could push the release into until early 2027. He subsequently reported in June that Apple had revised its chip roadmap, with the touchscreen MacBook Pro now expected to launch with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips instead of M6 Pro and M6 Max in an effort to keep the project on schedule.In a July report, Gurman reiterated that these laptops are planned for this fall, but a 2027 ship date is possible.


						

							


Which MacBook models will get a touchscreen? 
Current rumours suggest that Apple’s first touchscreen laptop will be a redesigned MacBook Pro with Pro and Max chips
Both Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman and analyst Ming-Chi Kuo have reported that Apple is developing MacBook Pro models with OLED touchscreen displays as part of a major redesign. The feature is expected to debut on the high-end MacBook Pro models powered by Apple’s Pro and Max chips, making them the first Macs to support direct touch input.
Apple is expected to use the touchscreen as a key differentiator for its professional laptops, further separating the MacBook Pro from the more affordable MacBook Air and MacBook Neo.
There is also speculation that Apple could rebrand the flagship model as the MacBook Ultra. According to one report from a source said to be familiar with Apple’s plans, the company intends to expand its “Ultra” branding beyond the Mac Studio and Apple silicon chips. However, this claim has not been corroborated by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman or analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, so it should be treated with caution.
For now, the technology appears set to remain exclusive to the MacBook Pro lineup. Neither the MacBook Air nor the MacBook Neo is expected to gain touchscreen support in the near term. However, Kuo believes Apple could eventually expand the technology to other MacBook models if the touchscreen MacBook Pro proves successful.
The MacBook Air may be the next candidate for a touchscreen upgrade, but current forecasts suggest this is unlikely before 2028 or 2029. Some reports also indicate that the Air could adopt OLED display technology before then, albeit without touch functionality.


						

							


Touchscreen MacBook Pro Design
Thinner than the current MacBook Pro
Punch hole for the FaceTime camera
Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro is expected to have a thinner, substantially lighter design. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has focused on reworking the internal layout and reducing and consolidating components to improve portability. No specific weight or thickness has been confirmed.
One of the most significant visual changes could be the removal of the display notch. Reports from display analysts and Bloomberg suggest Apple may replace the current notch with a hole-punch camera cutout, allowing for more usable screen space around the sensor. In early 2026, Gurman went a step further, claiming the new MacBook Pro could adopt an iPhone-like Dynamic Island interface built around the camera cutout.
The touchscreen MacBook Pro is also expected to retain its traditional laptop design, complete with a full keyboard and large trackpad, rather than becoming a hybrid tablet device.
Other rumoured design changes include:
A thinner and lighter chassis.
OLED display technology.
A hole-punch FaceTime camera replacing the notch.
Possible Dynamic Island-style functionality.
A reinforced hinge designed to minimise screen movement when the display is touched.
These changes would help distinguish the MacBook Pro from the MacBook Air and the entry-level MacBook Neo while giving Apple’s flagship laptop its most substantial design update in years.


						

							


Which chip will feature in the touchscreen MacBook?
M5 Pro and M5 Max
Early rumours suggested the touchscreen MacBook Pro would debut with Apple’s M6 Pro and M6 Max chips. However, more recent reports indicate that Apple has revised its plans and will instead launch the first touchscreen MacBook with M5 Pro and M5 Max processors before moving directly to the M7 generation.
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman in June 2026, Apple now plans to pair the redesigned MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than the previously rumoured M6 Pro and M6 Max. The report claims Apple may skip the M6 Pro/Max generation entirely to accelerate development of its AI-focused M7 chips, bringing them to market around six months earlier with significantly more powerful on-device AI capabilities.
While the ongoing DRAM and NAND shortages may also have influenced the decision, they are not thought to be the primary reason for the roadmap change. Apple has already raised Mac and iPad prices in response to higher memory costs.
The latest reports supersede earlier rumours that the touchscreen MacBook would feature M6-series processors built on TSMC’s 2nm process with a redesigned chip architecture. Leaked Apple files discovered by MacRumors in late 2025 also appeared to reference M6 MacBook Pro models, suggesting Apple was developing M6-based hardware before reportedly changing direction.
Separately, there has also been speculation that Apple could introduce its in-house 5G modem to a future MacBook Pro, enabling cellular connectivity without requiring Wi-Fi or an iPhone hotspot. However, this remains one of the least substantiated rumours surrounding the redesign.


						

							


Touchscreen MacBook Display
Tandem OLED display
Touchscreen interface
The display is expected to be the headline upgrade of Apple’s redesigned MacBook Pro. Multiple reports suggest Apple will replace the current Liquid Retina XDR (mini-LED) panel with a touchscreen OLED display, bringing MacBook Pro technology closer to the Ultra Retina XDR display used in the latest iPad Pro.
According to analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, Apple is planning to introduce OLED touch panels in the MacBook Pro in late 2026 or early 2027. The new display is expected to be thinner, more power-efficient, and capable of delivering deeper blacks, higher contrast, richer colours, and improved HDR performance than today’s mini-LED screens.
Reports indicate that both the 14-inch and 16-inch models will use advanced tandem OLED technology, which combines two OLED layers to achieve higher brightness levels while maintaining excellent energy efficiency. Apple first introduced this technology with the M4 iPad Pro and is expected to bring a similar implementation to the MacBook Pro.
The touchscreen functionality will reportedly rely on on-cell touch technology, which integrates touch sensors directly into the display rather than adding a separate layer. This approach helps keep the panel thin while supporting multi-touch input.
If the rumours prove accurate, the move to a tandem OLED touchscreen would represent the biggest display upgrade in the MacBook Pro’s history and one of the most significant changes to the lineup in years.

				
					

				
			
The iPad Pro has a TaNdem OLED display, the type of display that could make its way into the 2026 MacBook Pro.

Brady Snyder / Foundry



							


Touchscreen MacBook Interface 

				
					

				
			
macOS 27 could have some hidden touchscreen features. 

Foundry




Apple is not expected to turn macOS into iPadOS, but reports suggest macOS 27 could include subtle design changes to make the Mac easier to use with touch input.
Rather than replacing the traditional desktop experience, Apple is reportedly working on a touch-tuned interface that adapts depending on how the device is being used. When touch input is detected, interface elements such as menus, buttons, and controls may automatically enlarge to make them easier to tap. When using a mouse or trackpad, macOS would revert to its familiar point-and-click layout.
The touchscreen itself is expected to support standard gestures such as tapping, scrolling, and zooming, while still allowing users to switch between touch, trackpad, and mouse input.
Further clues appeared in the macOS 27.2 beta on October 5. MacRumors reported new code references to touch gestures in Safari, Photos, Notes and Quick Look. These could support a future touchscreen MacBook, but they could also relate to Sidecar, which allows an iPad to act as a Mac display. 


						

							


Touchscreen MacBook Pro: Connectivity 
5G connectivity could finally come to the Mac

				
					

				
			The C1X is now available,  but the C2 modem could be ready for the 2026 MacBook Pro.
Apple




Beyond the touchscreen display and redesigned chassis, one of the most intriguing rumours surrounding the next-generation MacBook Pro is built-in cellular connectivity.
Apple has spent the past several years developing its own modem technology, beginning with the C-series modem family. Reports suggest the company has explored bringing 5G connectivity to the MacBook lineup, allowing users to connect directly to mobile networks without relying on Wi-Fi or a smartphone hotspot.
Further evidence emerged in 2025 when Macworld contributor Filipe Esposito reported that Apple had tested an M5 MacBook Pro equipped with a 5G modem. While that feature did not make it into the final product, the report suggests Apple is actively evaluating cellular-enabled MacBooks.
The redesigned MacBook Pro could also benefit from Apple’s growing portfolio of wireless chips. The company’s N-series networking processors, which handle Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Thread connectivity, may eventually replace third-party components throughout the Mac lineup. An updated version of the chip could debut alongside the touchscreen MacBook Pro, improving power efficiency and tighter integration with Apple’s ecosystem.
While neither feature has been confirmed, Apple’s ongoing investment in modem and wireless technologies makes enhanced connectivity one of the more plausible additions to the redesigned MacBook Pro.


						

							


Touchscreen MacBook Pro: Price expectations
Apple will likely offer similar configurations to the current MacBook Pro models, but it’s unclear how much of a premium a touchscreen OLED display will command. Apple upped the price of the iPad Pro by $200 when it got a tandem OLED, so it’s likely the touchscreen MacBook Pro will have a higher starting price.

title: Tim Cook Explains Why He Stepped Down as Apple CEO Before iPhone Duo Launch
content:
The Independent's David Phelan on Wednesday interviewed Apple's executive chairman Tim Cook at Apple's U.K. headquarters in the Battersea Power Station, and one of the topics they discussed was John Ternus taking over as Apple's CEO.


Ternus, who was previously Apple's hardware engineering chief, succeeded Cook as Apple's CEO on September 1. Cook said the transition "started years ago."

"It's been an interesting transition," said Cook. "We really set out to have the best transition ever, a textbook example that people could look back to and learn from. It actually started years ago. Obviously, these things are not quick things and I feel so great about how things are going. I think everything has gone sort of exactly the way I had envisioned it. And it feels fantastic. Because Apple deserved the best."

iPhone Duo, in part to give Ternus some immediate momentum.

"I wanted John to have some wind at his back," said Cook. "And the wind at Apple is very much based on the product cycle. This product cycle feels unbelievably great. The Duo is coming in a few weeks and it's amazing."

Cook had the seemingly impossible task of succeeding the legendary Steve Jobs as CEO. Jobs told Cook not to make a decision simply because it is what Jobs would have done, and Cook said that he provided Ternus with similar advice.

"The advice I've given him is, make it your own job," said Cook. "Put your time in the things that you can add the most value to around the company. And that means don't mimic me. Just like I didn't mimic Steve. We all have different strengths."

title: 4 big announcements coming at Apple’s Welcome Home event
content:
Macworld





October is shaping up to be an exceptionally busy month at Apple Park. The company is readying the iPhone Duo, revamped Health app on iOS 27.2, touchscreen MacBook Pro, and overhauled iPad mini, which could all launch by the end of this month. That won’t be all.
Apple announced on Thursday that it will be holding a special “Welcome Home” experience on October 13, where it will presumably launch its new smart home products. According to credible rumors, the devices will include next-generation Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini models, along with a brand-new home hub. While many enthusiasts may perceive some of next week’s Apple TV and HomePod upgrades as unexciting performance boosts, the chip bumps will actually unlock never-before-seen advantages for Apple’s smart home line.
An all-new platform
The star of the show will undoubtedly be the dedicated home hub—what some are referring to as the HomePad. Hardware-related leaks and OS code references already give us a solid idea of what to expect from this forthcoming device, including its approximate size and some of its software perks.
The HomePad will offer a 6-inch, square-shaped touchscreen stitched to a HomePod-like speaker and draw AC power. Users will be able to display memories from their photo libraries when it’s idle—presumably depending on who’s detected nearby. It will rely on the built-in camera to recognize household members and surface apps/data accordingly, in addition to providing for FaceTime video calls.

				
					

				
			
Apple’s new smart platform is expected to use elements of the iPhone’s Standby mode when not in use.

Apple




Perhaps the most exciting aspect of the HomePad is the all-new homeOS, which will certainly introduce its own unique user interface and feature set to justify the creation of such a device. Apple TV 4K and HomePod models already act as HomeKit hubs, and the iPad is perfectly capable of controlling smart home accessories. So, it’s safe to assume that the HomePad will bring new features, enticing customers to add it to their existing setups.
Smarter speaker
The HomePod mini has been around for six years, providing a decent listening experience, seamless Apple ecosystem integrations, and basic voice command support in a miniature design. During the October 13 launch, Apple could finally unveil the HomePod mini 2, bringing fresh color options, potential audio improvements, and a faster S-series chip. While this may sound like an iterative upgrade, the HomePod mini 2 will finally resolve its predecessor’s main flaw.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Despite its smart speaker classification, the HomePod mini is currently powered by the classic Siri, which is anything but smart. The voice assistant frequently struggles to perform basic actions, requires precise phrasing, and instructs users to check their iPhones for complex answers. 
The HomePod mini 2 will address that by adopting Siri AI, allowing you to speak more naturally and get hands-free answers based on its trained data and your personal information. Many users will finally be satisfied with the HomePod’s overall performance, minimizing the need to hunt for smarter third-party alternatives like those from Google and Amazon.
A19 TV perks
Similar to the HomePod mini, the imminent Apple TV 4K 4’s most prominent highlight will be the introduction of a faster chip. First released in 2022, the current model packs the iPhone 13’s A15 Bionic chipset with 4GB of RAM. Next week’s model could bump that to an A19 or A19 Pro SoC from last year’s iPhone 17 lineup, increasing the RAM to 8GB or 12GB. This will bring Siri AI to the big screen and enhance the set-top box’s general performance. That seems unlikely to be the full story.
Opting for a year-old flagship smartphone processor in the midst of a chip shortage crisis solely for Siri AI support does not add up—especially since TVs aren’t primary AI consumption devices. Had it been the case, Apple could’ve easily repurposed the iPhone 15 Pro’s A17 Pro chip and gotten away with it.

				
					

				
			Apple wants you to game on your Apple TV, and a much better processor could help.
Foundry




As such, I presume the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K will bring meaningful software additions that take full advantage of the A19, like a more serious gaming push. Given that Beats has allegedly been developing game controllers, this theory could realistically materialize. Otherwise, no one is paying over two hundred bucks to stream Netflix and chill with Siri AI in the living room.
The great unknown
While iPhone hardware components tend to leak in advance all the time, Apple has a tighter grip over its software development teams. During pretty much every press event, the company surprises us with fresh OS features introductions that had been built in utter secrecy. These features often roll out to older devices, too, despite being marketed for the latest and greatest releases.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




So even if you’re not planning to upgrade your current Apple smart home devices, the next software update could still elevate your experience with significant additions—like iOS 27.2’s four-HomePod surround sound setup.

title: Apple sets NYC ‘experience’ next week to showcase new smart home devices
content:
Macworld





It’s official. Apple will announce its big push into the smart home on Tuesday, October 13. This isn’t expected to be a big special event keynote at Apple Park, but rather a web launch with a coordinated “Special Experience” for invited members of the media to go hands-on with the new products in New York City.
Apple did the same thing with the launch of the MacBook Neo earlier this year, after wrapping up a week of product announcements. That launch followed three days of announcements; however, this time everything is expected to drop at the same time. Apple’s Senior VP of Marketing Greg Joswiak posted a video showing the creation of the embroidered Apple logo and “Welcome Home” tagline.
So what is Apple expected to announce? Reportedly, we’re getting a trio of new products: An updated Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini with new processors that make them suitable to run Siri AI, and the headline device, an all-new home hub device.
The Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini are expected to be relatively straightforward updates with new chips to enable Apple Intelligence features and a few minor tweaks, such as HomePod mini colors, but without any dramatic design or interface changes. It’s the new home hub device that is the star of the show.
Apple’s answer to the Amazon Echo Show or Google Nest Hub, this new as-yet-unnamed device (most call it “HomePad” for now) is a totally new thing, with a new design, operating system, and interface. The most reliable rumors say it has a 6-inch display with a squareish aspect ratio, attached via a polished metal arm to a half-dome perforated base similar in size to a HomePod mini. Like a tiny little iMac G4.
It will have a new operating system and a new interface that is supposedly a mashup of tvOS, iOS widgets, iPhone Standby mode, and Apple Watch faces and complications. You’ll be able to access your smart home controls as well as your calendar, messages, Apple Music and Podcasts, and make FaceTime calls thanks to the forward-facing camera. That camera reportedly has a cool new trick, too: recognizing which user is looking at it and switching to their own preferences and showing their own data.
In addition to Apple’s trio of new products, it might show off some smart home stuff made in partnership with other manufacturers. Apple is said to have partnered with LG on a set of smart home products: A doorbell, an indoor camera, an outdoor camera, and an outdoor floodlight cam. These will carry LG branding, but were designed in conjunction with Apple, so Apple will likely show some of these products on October 13 as well.
The media event to accompany this “Welcome Home” launch is on Tuesday, October 13 at 9:00 am ET in New York. It’s not clear whether Apple will accompany this with a longer keynote-style video to introduce these products, as it does with other events, or if it will simply launch new product pages directly on the Apple website.

title: Apple event guide: October ‘experience’ is confirmed
content:
Macworld





Apple’s September event may not have been Apple’s final event of 2026. Apple has confirmed a special “Welcome home” Experience for Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at 9am ET (2pm BST). Selected journalists have been invited to attend the gathering in New York, suggesting Apple is preparing to introduce new products focused on the smart home.
Apple hasn’t confirmed what it will announce, but rumors point to its long-awaited HomePad smart display, a new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV 4K. The gathering could follow the format of Apple’s March Experience, with product announcements made separately and journalists invited to try the new devices.
Apple typically has four main event windows each year: a spring event, WWDC in June, the iPhone event in September, and sometimes a further event in October. The company rarely confirms dates far in advance, and there’s no guarantee it will hold an event in every window. That leaves Apple fans – and anyone considering a new Apple device – wondering when the next event will happen and what might be announced. Fortunately, Apple’s annual schedule is fairly predictable, while reliable rumours often provide additional clues about what’s coming. That means we can make informed estimates about the timing of future keynotes and the products most likely to appear.
Here’s everything we know about the next event Apple will hold – and beyond.


When is Apple’s next event?
Next Apple Experience: October 13, 2026. Confirmed by Greg Joswiak on X. 
Apple’s Greg Joswiak has indicated on X that an Apple ‘event’ – or rather a ‘Special Experience’ will take place on Tuesday, October 13. 
The theme appears to be “Welcome Home”, as you can see from this image: 

				
					

				
			
Apple




Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman had claimed on X that Apple would launch its “next big thing” on October 13, referring to new smart-home products. 
The last time Apple held an October event was the “Scary Fast” event that took place on October 30, 2023.


						

							


What could Apple launch at the next event?
The rumored lineup centers on Apple’s first smart-home display, often called HomePad. Gurman describes a 6-inch screen mounted above a speaker base on a manually tilting arm, plus a separate wall-mounted version. Updated HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K models with faster processors are also expected.
Other rumored launches include new iPads and a touchscreen MacBook Pro, but this report does not establish that they will arrive alongside the smart-home products.


						

							




Apple event calendar 2026: What has Apple launched this year?


TimescaleEvent themeDatesProducts

March Special Experience2-4 MarchLaunched: iPhone 17e, MacBooks Neo, Pro & Air, iPad Air
JuneWWDCJune 8Unveiled plans for: iOS, macOS, other software, AI and Siri
SeptemberiPhone eventSeptember 9Launched: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Duo, new Apple Watch, AirPods 5
OctoberApple Experience: Welcome homeOctober 13 (date confirmed)Possible: HomePad, HomePod mini, Apple TV
Late 2026Other possible announcementsUnconfirmedPossible: Touchscreen MacBook, iPads
Spring 2027TBCTBCExpected: iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2

 



Apple has held three events so far in 2026, although the first was not an event in the traditional sense. On March 4, the company invited select media to hands-on “experiences” in multiple locations. In the run-up to that date, Apple launched several products via press release, including the iPhone 17e, M4 iPad Air, and M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pro, M5 MacBook Air and the MacBook Neo.
The second event was WWDC, which began with a keynote on June 8. At the WWDC keynote Apple outlined the upcoming changes to its operating systems, including iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate.
In August Apple issued press releases to announce the new Mac mini and Mac Studio. 
At the September 9 event Apple unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, a foldable iPhone Duo, a new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and AirPods 5. 

				
					

				
			
Calendars at the ready.

Foundry





 FAQ 


1.
How far in advance does Apple announce an event?
Apple usually announces its events around one to two weeks before they take place, although the timing varies. The October 13, 2026 Experience was announced just five days in advance. Apple also sometimes chooses to announce products via press release without holding an event. 





2.
What time does the next Apple event start in U.S., U.K. and other global time zones
Apple has invites some members of the media to an “Apple Experience” in Tribeca, New York on October 13 at 9:00 am (6am PT / 2pm BST)
That timing differs to Apple’s usual events, which start at 10am PT or 1pm ET. 
Apple keynotes usually start at 10 am PT. A future event would likely follow the same pattern. That translates to the following times in the countries where most of our readers live:
U.S.: 10 am PDT, 11 am MDT, 12 pm CDT, 1 pm EDT
Canada: as above, plus 2 pm ADT
U.K.: 6 pm
Europe: 7 pm CEST, 8 pm EEST
India: 10:30 pm IST
Australia: next day — 1 am AWST, 2:30 am ACST, 3 am AEST
New Zealand: next day — 5 am NZST
The timings are generally the same for all Apple Keynotes, but can be slightly different if Apple holds the event during the period of a couple of weeks when the clocks have changed in the U.S. but not elsewhere (in 2026 the clocks will change in the U.S. on November 1, while in the U.K. they change on October 25).
Sometimes Apple holds events at different times, for example, in October 2023 the event was held in late afternoon in San Francisco, which meant it was midnight in the U.K. 
If Apple doesn’t hold an event and instead just issues a press release, that usually happens around 8 am PT, 11 am ET and 4 pm U.K. time.





3.
How long do Apple events usually last?
Apple keynotes usually last between one and two hours and feature the CEO alongside various other Apple executives. We don’t anticipate a Keynote at the October Experience. 
WWDC and the September event tend to be longer keynotes; the spring and late-fall events can be slightly shorter.
For example, the September 2024 event was 1 hour 38 minutes.





4.
How often does Apple hold events?
There can be as many as four Apple events in a year:  
Spring Event
WWDC in June
iPhone Event in September
Late Fall Event in October
This event calendar is by no means set in stone, though, with the spring and October events being less regular. Some years, Apple doesn’t hold a spring event at all. In 2025 Apple only held two events, preferring instead to announce new products via press release.





5.
Will there be a live stream at the next Apple Event?
Add that Apple hasn’t confirmed a public livestream of the October 13 Experience, but it may make video presentations available following the event. This is likely to take the same format as the March Experiences. 





6.
Does Apple ever announce products without an event? 
Apple frequently announces products without a keynote event, often opting for press releases or multi-day announcement windows. In recent years, the company has increasingly reserved its large-scale media events for major flagship launches, such as the primary iPhone lineup in September, while using press releases for iterative updates or “chip bumps” that may not warrant a full hour-long presentation.





7.
How to watch an Apple event
Apple has not confirmed whether its October 13 Experience will be livestreamed. Unlike a traditional keynote, the gathering could be a hands-on showcase for invited journalists, with announcements published separately on Apple’s website.
Apple events are typically broadcast across several digital platforms, allowing viewers to tune in from almost any device. While the company previously restricted access to its own hardware or the Safari browser, these barriers have been removed in recent years.
You can access live Apple presentations through the following official channels:
YouTube: This is often considered the easiest way to watch. Apple streams its keynotes live on its official YouTube channel, which can be accessed via any web browser or the YouTube app on smartphones, tablets, and smart TVs.
Apple.com: The company hosts a dedicated “Events” page on its official website. For the best experience on a PC, it is recommended to use Microsoft Edge on Windows 10 or later.
Apple TV App: The stream is available within the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV hardware. Keynotes are usually listed in the app’s lineup a day or two before the event begins.
Apple Podcasts: Apple also showcases its events through the Podcasts app on Apple devices, where you can watch the video presentation.
You may also like to tune in to our Live Blog which will provide minute-by-minute text updates and analysis as products are announced.
Following the end of the event, detailed breakdowns will also be available on the Macworld Podcast, which can be found on Spotify, Soundcloud, and Apple Podcasts. 








Will Apple have a October event in 2026?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple appears to be gearing up for a smart-home launch on October 13. The company is hosting selected media at an ‘Apple Experience’ in New York from 9am that day. This event appears to be similar format to Apple’s March launches. 
The last time Apple held a late fall event was on October 30, 2023, and before that on October 18, 2021. So while a late fall event would not be unprecedented, it has become relatively uncommon.
What to expect from Apple’s October 13 Experience?
Apple’s October 13 launch could feature smart-home products, including the rumored HomePad smart display, an updated HomePod mini and a new Apple TV 4K. The HomePod mini and Apple TV are expected to gain faster processors that could support Siri AI features. It is not yet clear whether all three products would arrive together.
Other possible announcements before the end of 2026 include the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro and updates to the iPad and iPad mini. These could launch separately, and their rumored timing does not confirm that Apple will hold another event.
For more on the possible timing and products, read: Apple’s October event: Latest rumors and what to expect.


						

							


Will Apple hold a spring event in 2027? 

				
					

				
			John Ternus: Apple’s new CEO.
Michael Simon / Foundry




Apple’s spring events have become increasingly unpredictable. The company has not held a traditional spring event since May 2024, although it did invite members of the media, including Macworld, to a “Special Apple Experience” in 2026. 
Rather than a keynote presentation, the March 4, 2026 gathering was a hands-on showcase that followed three days of product announcements, including the MacBook Neo, iPhone 17e, and M5 MacBook Air.
Will Apple take a similar approach to spring product launches in 2027? It’s certainly possible. The format appeared to work well, allowing each product announcement to receive its own media coverage rather than competing for attention during a single event. 
Apple is expected to release three iPhone models in spring 2027 – or it could be two new iPhones, with the Air and iPhone 18 merging.
iPhone 18 (base model)
iPhone 18e
iPhone Air 2
Apple may also update the MacBook Air with an M6 processor in spring 2027. 


						

							


When is WWDC 2027?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




When is the WWDC keynote?
In 2026 the WWDC keynote was on Monday June 8. In 2025 it started on Monday June 9. We expect WWDC will start on Monday 7 June in 2027. 
WWDC generally runs from the Monday to Friday in the second week of June. 
What Apple could launch at WWDC
WWDC is Apple’s big developer event at which it reveals plans for the operating systems that run on Apple hardware.
In June 2027 we expect Apple to unveil details of iOS 28, iPadOS 28, macOS 28, updates to watchOS, tvOS, HomePod software, and an update to Apple’s realityOS.
Apple sometimes announces new hardware at WWDC, usually the high-end models targeted at power users, so we could see new Macs.
Following the keynote on Monday, developer events and sessions will run throughout the week. You can read more about WWDC date, times and everything you need to know in a separate article.


						

							


What did Apple launch at past events?
So far in 2026 Apple has held an ‘experience’, which rather than being an event in the traditional sense, was a chance for journalists to get a look at products Apple had launched in the days prior, including MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e. The company also hosted the WWDC keynote on June 8, at which it revealed its plans for Apple Intelligence and Siri in iOS 27, macOS 27 and the other operating systems. Plus Apple held its iPhone launch event on September 9 at which the iPhone 18 Pro and Max, iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and AirPods 5 launched. 
In 2025 Apple only held two events. The first was its Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) on June 9, at which it introduced the new features coming in the next version of its operating systems, and the second was the huge September 9 Apple Event where it launched new Apple Watches, new AirPods Pro and the new iPhones for 2025.
Apple doesn’t have to hold an event to launch new products though. Prior to WWDC, Apple launched a new iPhone 16e via press release on February 19, a new iPad and iPad Air via press release on March 4, and a new MacBook Air and Mac Studio on March 5. 
Apple then went on to launch a new M5 MacBook Pro and M5 iPad Pro in October. No event was held to mark these launches.
In 2024, Apple held three events: one on Tuesday, May 7, at which it launched new iPads; a keynote to kick off WWDC on June 10; and an event on September 9 at which Apple unveiled the new iPhone 16, Apple Watch Series 10 and the AirPods 4. In October 2024 there was no event, but Apple did announce new products (iMac, Mac mini and MacBook Pro) via press release.
In 2023 there were three events: WWDC in June, an iPhone event in September, and Apple’s second fall event on October 30 (or after midnight on October 31 if you weren’t in the U.S.).
In 2022 Apple held three events: a spring event on March 8, WWDC on June 6, and the iPhone 14 launch on September 7. In other years Apple has held four events though.

				
					

				
			
Foundry



							


When were Apple’s past events?

title: Go grab these Mac deals before Amazon remembers to raise the prices

Everything is more expensive nowadays, including Macs. The higher prices have an effect on our shopping habits, so you might be more inclined to take advantage of a sale price as soon as you see one, instead of waiting for a better deal. After all, there’s a good chance prices will go up again, since the supply shortage isn’t going to ease up anytime soon.
Today is the last day of Amazon’s fall sales event, and that includes Macs. We weren’t expecting much, but you can save a good chunk of change on many Mac models during the event, and there are a few Macs that are actually really good deals. Here are the Amazon Mac deals you should pick up before time runs out.
And if Macs aren’t your thing, be sure to check out all the Best Prime Day Apple deals.

When Apple released the M6 Mac mini, it raised prices on top of the June hikes, bringing the entry-level model to a depressing $899. But today, Amazon is selling the base M6 Mac mini for $780, a savings of $119 (13 percent) off Apple’s price. It only has 16GB of RAM and a 256GB SSD, which probably isn’t enough for AI development, but you can also save up to $150 on models with more storage and memory, so go check it out.
Mac mini on Amazon U.S.

Also, the 20 percent performance boost of M6 over the M5 doesn’t have the same value as it used to, so you’re safe grabbing this Amazon deal before time runs out.

Now, perhaps you’re waiting for the imminent OLED MacBook Pro upgrade, which could happen soon. title: Amazon Unveils New iPad Rivals With Alexa+ and Google Play
content:
Amazon today announced a new lineup of Alexa Tablets, introducing three aluminum tablets with Google Play access, integrated Alexa+, and prices starting at $229.99 to compete with Apple's iPad lineup.


The new tablets run Android, moving away from Amazon's Fire OS and its separate app store. Google Play support brings access to apps such as YouTube, Gmail, and Google Docs, addressing a longstanding limitation of Amazon's tablets.

iPad Pro at a significantly lower price point. It features a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 chip, a 12-inch display with an adaptive refresh rate of up to 120Hz and a 3:2 aspect ratio, a 6.5mm-thick aluminum body, Wi-Fi 6E, and quad Dolby Atmos speakers. Amazon is also introducing a $149.99 Pro Keyboard and $89.99 Pro Pen for the 12-inch model. Both attach magnetically, while the keyboard includes a trackpad and connects without Bluetooth pairing. title: Intego ONE Review: Top-tier Mac malware protection with powerful Firewall controls
content:
Macworld





At a glance
Expert's Rating



Pros
Malware detection that caught nearly every threat 
Fast scan speeds, processing 700GB+ and millions of files in under 10 minutes
Strong, granular firewall controls with easy allow/deny/edit rule management
Easy-to-use iPhone VPN with useful security checks
Cons
Lacks web/phishing protection and parental controls
Slow quarantine cleanup 
iPhone app lacks advanced VPN features
Our Verdict 
Intego ONE offers superb malware detection, excellent firewall controls, and impressively fast scan times, even across millions of files. Recent updates have improved performance during cleanup and resolved several frustrating bugs. It still lacks features such as spam and phishing prevention, and a few interface limitations remain, but it’s a strong choice for Mac users who want reliable malware protection and excellent network control at a good price. The Complete plan also includes an iPhone app with a straightforward VPN and useful security checks, although it lacks some advanced features found in dedicated VPN apps.

Intego (annual) 
											
$29.99					
View Deal					
Who it’s best for: Mac users who want strong, reliable malware protection with advanced control over network activity should seriously consider Intego ONE Complete. It’s especially suited to users who prioritize security performance over having an all-in-one feature set.
Who it’s not for: It’s missing key features you’d expect at this price, like phishing protection and parental controls, so if you need those features look elsewhere. 
At a glance
Protection: ★★★★★
Performance: ★★★★★
Features: ★★★★☆
Ease of use: ★★★★★
Value: ★★★★☆
Intego ONE is Intego’s new antivirus and anti-malware package, replacing Internet Security X9. We have long recommended its predecessor as the best antivirus utility for Mac users, thanks to its excellent malware detection, strong ransomware protection, and tools designed specifically for macOS. Intego ONE improves on it in several respects.
There are three plans available, with options covering one, three, or five Macs. Intego ONE Complete also includes an iPhone for each Mac covered by the subscription.
Intego ONE Essential: Antivirus protection and a firewall.
Intego ONE Advanced: Adds SmartClean to free up disk space and remove junk files. 
Intego ONE Complete: Adds Intego VPN and an iPhone app with VPN access, network speed tests, and security checks.  
We tested Intego ONE Complete, including its Antivirus, Firewall, VPN, and SmartClean modules, as well as the companion iPhone app. Each Mac module has its own features and customization options, while the iPhone app provides additional VPN and security tools.
Intego ONE requires macOS 12.4 Monterey or later and is easy to set up. Like previous versions, it asks for full disk access and permission to create a network extension for firewall and filtering functions.
Antivirus: How good is Intego ONE Complete at detecting malware?

				
					

				
			
An Intego ONE Complete Quick Scan in progress
.
Foundry




Perhaps the strongest feature of the package, Intego ONE’s antivirus module took just about everything I threw at it from over 130 viral samples from the Objective-See malware collection and came out smiling. 
Scan performance improved dramatically with version 1.2.3 (compared to our initial tests of the Release Candidate), with the software processing more than two million files in roughly eight minutes in testing – placing it among the fastest options currently available for macOS. 
The software, which offers Full Scan, Quick Scan, and Custom Scan options, dovetailed in perfectly with the Xprotect/Gatekeeper tools found in macOS Tahoe 26.4, issued warnings, and prevented malware and ransomware from being installed on all fronts.

				
					

				
			
Intego ONE quickly plowed through and removed more than 200 quarantined files, but left three behind.

Foundry




What few exceptions did get through via developer tools such as Xcode or Visual Code were caught moments later, and where I thought a fake copy of the Transmission BitTorrent client had gotten through, Intego ONE flagged it and quickly removed it via quarantine. Even fake Flash Player applications, which have long been the bane of antivirus utilities, were stopped immediately, and the software came through with flying colors while also scanning my MacBook Pro’s SSD, complete with more than 877GB of data, in under 10 minutes.
Other nifty features from the Antivirus module included a Custom Scan feature, which was well-implemented and included targeted scanning as well as an excellent auto-scan feature in which a test flash drive with malware on it was quickly scanned and its suspect files quarantined. A handy scheduling feature worked like a charm, and it’s easy to configure a set daily, weekly, or monthly scan as needed.
Firewall: How much control does the firewall actually give you?

				
					

				
			
Quickly editing a Firewall function and assigning an application to a function.

Foundry




Intego ONE’s firewall feature may not be as customizable as a systems administrator might like, but what’s present is on point, complete with readily accessible configuration options that allow for a network connection and allow it to be denied or edited on the fly.
One of the first things you’ll notice after installing the software is how active the firewall itself is, reminding you of network connections as they emerge and asking whether you approve them or if they might be suspicious.
New rules can be created on the fly, and easy scripting allows you to activate applications on your Mac to deal with them as well as add a network port. A list of currently approved networks is available, and you can see which servers your Mac is trying to talk to and get a bead on your overall network traffic.
VPN: Is the built-in VPN good enough to use daily?
With the Intego ONE Complete plan you can take advantage of a VPN. This VPN may not be as robust as a dedicated VPN app, but what’s present is robust and has a good level of customization. Just click into the module from the home screen, activate the VPN, and it’s easy to geolocate to one of 51 servers around the world, as well as choose favorites.
Interestingly, the VPN module offers a choice between your preferred VPN module, wherein you can choose between Lightway – UPD, which is optimized for speed, and Lightway – TCP, which is optimized for reliability. Where performance itself was concerned, the bandwidth proved excellent, and the frame rates and audio sync on streaming content proved excellent.
Intego ONE Complete also extends VPN protection to the iPhone, although the iOS app has fewer configuration options than its Mac counterpart. Here’s how it performed in our tests.
What does Intego ONE for iPhone do?

				
					

				
			
VPN location selection and Security assessment 
 
Foundry




Intego ONE for iOS is a mobile companion to Intego ONE Complete for Mac, combining a VPN with a selection of security and privacy checks. It doesn’t offer the full antivirus and firewall protection found in the Mac version, but it provides useful tools for keeping your iPhone’s internet connection private and checking important security settings.
The app requires iOS 18.2 or later and is available through the App Store. Installation is straightforward: download the app, sign in to your Intego account, and allow it to create a VPN configuration. Once that’s done, you’re ready to use the VPN and security tools.
Is the VPN any good on iPhone?
The VPN client makes it easy to switch between international servers and create a favorites list for locations you use regularly. Connections and disconnections are quick, and the app performed well in our tests over both Wi-Fi and cellular connections.
One limitation is that the iPhone app currently supports only the WireGuard VPN protocol. This gives users fewer configuration options than the Mac version, although it shouldn’t be an issue for most people who just want a simple VPN connection.
We tested Intego ONE on an iPhone 17 running iOS 27.0.1, using both Wi-Fi and AT&T’s 5G network. Tests were conducted with Ookla’s Speedtest.net app and Intego’s built-in speed test tool.
On Wi-Fi, our download speed averaged 84.1Mbps without a VPN, dropping to 71.9Mbps when connected to a Canadian server and 71.3Mbps with a New York server. That’s a reduction of around 15%, leaving plenty of bandwidth for streaming and other everyday activities.
The impact was greater over cellular. Our average download speed fell from 289.4Mbps without a VPN to 179.2Mbps through Canada and 174.8Mbps through New York, a reduction of approximately 38% to 40%. Nevertheless, these speeds remained more than adequate for streaming and large file transfers.
Intego’s built-in speed test reported average download speeds of 70.3Mbps over Wi-Fi and 139Mbps over cellular.
Streaming worked smoothly during testing, with good video quality, and the iPhone maintained a reasonable temperature even when streaming on battery power.
What security features does Intego ONE offer on iPhone?
Beyond its VPN, Intego ONE provides a useful security checkup. It can remind you to review whether important iPhone protections are enabled, including Face ID, your passcode, and the latest iOS updates.
The app also checks settings relating to ad tracking, detects whether screen recording is active, and looks for signs of jailbreaking, which can weaken Apple’s built-in security protections.
Intego ONE can also check the security of the Wi-Fi network your iPhone is connected to. The check takes around 10 seconds and identifies potential security issues, including whether the network uses strong encryption. It also reports connection speed, which can be useful when connecting to unfamiliar networks in hotels, cafés, or airports.
These tools are helpful reminders, particularly if you don’t regularly review your iPhone’s security and privacy settings. However, they don’t replace active threat protection. Intego ONE for iOS won’t prevent you from visiting a malicious website or clicking a phishing link, and it doesn’t provide the traditional antivirus and malware-scanning capabilities found in Intego ONE for Mac.
Is Intego ONE for iPhone worth using?
Intego ONE for iPhone is a useful addition to the Complete package. Its VPN is easy to configure, switching servers is straightforward, and performance was good enough for everyday use, including streaming.
It’s less suitable for users who want the extensive customization offered by dedicated VPN services, including more protocol choices and an internet kill switch. The security checks are useful, but they’re reminders to review your settings rather than comprehensive protection against online threats.
If you’re already subscribing to Intego ONE Complete for your Mac, the iPhone app is a worthwhile extra. It provides an easy way to use a VPN on the go while encouraging better security habits, without needing to learn another complicated security app.
For more on VPNs read our group test of the best VPNs for iPhone and iPad. 
SmartClean: Is SmartClean a good Mac cleaner?
The SmartClean module is included with the Intego ONE Advanced and Intego ONE Complete plans. It’s a tool for disk optimization and offers several functions to manage CPU usage, RAM usage, a Disk Space Monitor, an App Uninstaller, and Optimization history.
Each function works well, and the overall SmartClean Optimization Scan was able to locate 111GB of large files on my Mac that could be removed, as well as 500MB of cache and log files. It is a good way to claw back some drive space without decimating your larger work files.
This disk cleanup can be extended in the settings to also include old downloads and old trash files, which is a nice option.
The Uninstaller function worked well and cleanly removed several extraneous applications I had on my SSD, but an attempt to remove a copy of DaVinci Resolve during a test run had to be repeated. This is one of a few bugs that cropped up in our testing of the Release Candidate, so we raised these issue with Intego and will be verifying that it has been addressed in the final version of the software.
What is missing?
Parental controls and spam/phishing protection would be good to see in a future update.
What issues and bugs did we encounter?

				
					

				
			
Quarantining suspect files in Intego ONE.

Foundry




While Intego ONE Complete is generally excellent and its component functions shine, there are still a few quirks and interface limitations to note, though several earlier issues identified in our initial review have been resolved.
The application no longer repeatedly prompts for the system password during quarantine or malware removal, which was a major annoyance in earlier builds. Performance during large-scale cleanup has also improved considerably, with better system load distribution preventing the Mac from slowing to a crawl.
During testing, the software successfully processed and removed more than 200 quarantined files quickly, though a small number of files (three in our case) remained and required additional attention.
The user interface, while generally friendly, still lacks the ability to resize or expand to full screen, which feels like an unnecessary limitation.
A previous issue involving the application resetting permissions and requiring reinstallation did not reoccur in this version, suggesting it may have been resolved.
Pricing: Is Intego ONE good value?
Intego ONE Essential starts $2.50/£1.87 a month for one device for the first year, after that first year it will default to the full price of $3.33/£2.50 a month. That’s $29.99/£22.49 for the first year and then $39.99/£29.99 a year. You can choose a two year plan to keep paying the lower price for longer.
Get the best Intego ONE deal here 
Intego ONE Advanced (with the Mac cleaner) is currently $52.49/£38.49 for the first year, and Intego ONE Complete (with the VPN) is $67.49/£45.49 for the first year. There are plans for one, three or five devices.
Intego ONE Complete also includes the iPhone app, with plans covering one Mac and one iPhone, three Macs and three iPhones, or five Macs and five iPhones. The iPhone app includes VPN access, network speed tests, and security checks, but not the Mac version’s antivirus and firewall features.
In comparison to Intego’s Mac Internet Security X9, which though available for $24.99/£20.99 for the first year, rose to $49.99/£49.99 a year afterwards, the new pricing structure is better for the long-term. The price is also very favourable compared to alternatives we include in our round up of the Best Antivirus software for Mac users. 

				
					

				
			

Foundry




Should you buy Intego ONE?
Intego ONE proves to be an easy recommendation if you’re looking for strong malware protection and advanced firewall control on your Mac, and this is where the application shines.
Recent updates have addressed several early bugs and significantly improved performance, making Intego ONE a more compelling option than at launch. 
The addition of an iPhone app makes the Complete package more appealing if you want protection for both your Mac and iPhone. While the iOS app doesn’t offer the same antivirus capabilities as the Mac version, its straightforward VPN delivered good performance in our tests, and the security checks provide useful reminders. It’s a worthwhile addition rather than a reason to subscribe on its own.
Where core protection is concerned, this is one of the best options available for your Mac, and this, combined with Intego’s 30-day money-back guarantee, makes it well worth a trial run.
